name: Tirzepatide
drug_class: Dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist ('twincretin')
route_note: subcutaneous injection once weekly (2.5–15 mg) by pen or vial

discovery.note: A 39-amino-acid peptide based on the GIP sequence, engineered to also activate the GLP-1 receptor, with a C20 fatty diacid for albumin binding.

tagline: First dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist, giving about 20% weight loss in obesity trials
summary: Tirzepatide is a once-weekly injectable peptide that activates both the GIP and GLP-1 receptors. It produces larger reductions in HbA1c and body weight than selective GLP-1 agonists, with mean weight loss around 20% in the SURMOUNT-1 obesity trial, and is approved for type 2 diabetes, obesity and obstructive sleep apnoea.
mechanism: Tirzepatide is a GIP-based peptide that is a full agonist at the GIP receptor and a biased partial agonist at the GLP-1 receptor (favouring cAMP signalling with less receptor internalisation). Both incretin pathways increase glucose-dependent insulin secretion; GLP-1 activity also lowers glucagon and slows gastric emptying.

Central actions on appetite reduce energy intake, and GIP receptor activation in adipose tissue may improve lipid handling and insulin sensitivity. A C20 fatty diacid moiety binds albumin, giving a half-life of about five days.
uses: Chronic weight management in obesity or overweight with comorbidity (Zepbound/Mounjaro)
Moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea in adults with obesity (Zepbound)

history.title: SURPASS-2
history.detail: Tirzepatide outperforms semaglutide 1 mg on HbA1c and weight in type 2 diabetes (NEJM 2021).

history.title: Mounjaro approved
history.detail: FDA approves Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes in May 2022; SURMOUNT-1 reports up to 20.9% mean weight loss.

history.title: Zepbound
history.detail: FDA approves Zepbound for chronic weight management in November 2023.

history.title: Sleep apnoea; shortage resolved
history.detail: FDA approves Zepbound for obstructive sleep apnoea (December); FDA declares the tirzepatide shortage resolved.

history.title: Head-to-head and outcomes trials
history.detail: SURMOUNT-5 shows greater weight loss than semaglutide 2.4 mg, and SURPASS-CVOT reports cardiovascular non-inferiority versus dulaglutide.

pk.metabolism: proteolysis, beta-oxidation of the fatty diacid and amide hydrolysis

serious: reduced oral contraceptive efficacy after dose changes
safety.boxed_warning: Risk of thyroid C-cell tumours: caused C-cell tumours in rodents; contraindicated with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.

facts: Tirzepatide was the first dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist to be approved.
SURMOUNT-1 reported a mean 20.9% weight reduction at 72 weeks with the 15 mg dose.
